column2: "Townsville Bulletin (Australia) March 30, 2021 Tuesday Townsville Edition Copyright 2021 Nationwide News Pty Limited All Rights Reserved Section: NATION; Pg. 12 Length: 259 words Byline: James Morrow Body A CHINESE diplomat has taken aim at the sex scandals engulfing Canberra, claiming that \"international investigations\" need to be held to hold parliament to account. Li Yang, China's consul-general in Rio de Janeiro, tweeted: \"The cases of sexual crimes happened in the Australian parliament are shocking! This relates to the protection of women's human rights. Australia should accept unrestricted international investigations into those cases.\" Mr Li's tweet comes amidst growing questions about China's human rights abuses of its Uighyur population, and is seen as a swipe at Australia's push for an international investigation into the origins of the coronavirus. It also comes just four months after a major diplomatic stoush between China and Australia prompted by another of Beijing's diplomats publishing a photoshopped image of an Australian soldier holding a knife to an Afghan child's throat. \"Who knew? Officials in the Chinese Communist Party have a sense of humour,\" said academic and author Clive Hamilton when shown the tweet by Mr Li (pictured). \"I wonder if the women being raped in Xinjiang's concentration camps agree,\" he said. China has been criticised for its human rights violations and lack of transparency on issues including the coronavirus pandemic. China allowed a WHO delegation to investigate the origins of the coronavirus earlier this year but no conclusions were reached. Beijing has also refused access to United Nations investigators wishing to visit Xinjiang province, where the regime has been accused of cultural genocide.
